newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French CGIP buys into car parts maker Valeo. [CORRECTED 13:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French CGIP buys into car parts maker Valeo. [CORRECTED 13:32 GMT]

text.p: French holding company CGIP said on Tuesday it was buying 20 percent of car parts manufacturer Valeo to become the leading shareholder in a group which the country's car makers have fought tooth and nail to keep in French hands.

Cerus, a holding company owned by Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti, sold the 20 percent stake to CGIP, and is selling 3.6 percent to French state bank CDC, plus 3.6 percent more to U.S. investment fund JP Morgan GT Corporation for a total of at least 6.5 billion francs ($1.27 billion). (Corrects from "...plus 3.6 percent more to U.S. investment bank JP Morgan and GT Corporation)

Valeo, Europe's second largest parts maker and a leading supplier of French and German carmakers, said it would also make an advance 1996 dividend downpayment of 10 francs for which Cerus would still be beneficiary.
The deal also involves another payout of 10 francs per share to Cerus if Valeo's 1997 net attributable profit is at least equal to 1.45 billion francs, a statement from Cerus said.
All three firms issued statements and were holding news conferences on Tuesday morning.

Cerus said it would use the proceeds partly to pay off debts and would continue to divest financial and property assets while pursuing a strategy of taking controlling stakes in industrial and services groups.

It said the sale of its 28 percent stake was at 330 francs per share. This would raise 6.3 billion francs and the advance dividend downpayment would generate a further 0.2 billion. The further conditional dividends tied to 1997 profits at Valeo would generate another 0.2 billion, it added.
Under the deal, the state-owned bank Caisse des Depots et Consignation (CDC) will take its Valeo stake to 5.4 percent from 1.9 percent.
The acquisition by CGIP will be welcome news for the French government as well as carmakers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen.
They had all been seeking ways to ensure Valeo stayed out of foreign hands.
CGIP recently announced that it had raised around 3.2 billion francs through the sale of a stake in U.S. company Crown Cork and Seal, which will help pay for the Valeo stake.

The stake has been up for grabs for more than a year since de Benedetti first made it known he was looking to sell as he sought fresh finances for the Italian computer group Olivetti, from which he has since resigned as chairman.

News that his Cerus French holding company was ready to sell caused consternation in French car industry circles amid reports of interest from U.S. giants Delphi Automotive Systems, which belongs to General Motors, and TRW Inc.

Threats of a boycott by the French car manufacturers which are Valeo's biggest clients is thought to have discouraged any foreign bids. Among the most vociferous supporters of keeping Valeo French was PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet.
CGIP, Compagnie Generale d'Industrie et de Participations, previously held a stake in Valeo but sold it in 1993.
It has a string of investments in the industrial and information technology spheres.
